subject: Chemistry
title: Hennig Brand Discovers Phosphorus
description: Learn Hennig Brand Discovers Phosphorus in one minute.

hook.text: In 1669, a German alchemist boiled 1,500 gallons of urine and accidentally discovered a new element.

buildup.text: Hennig Brand was searching for the philosopher's stone. He thought gold might hide in human urine.

discovery.text: After weeks of boiling and heating, a waxy substance glowed in the dark. He had found phosphorus.

twist.text: Brand kept it secret to profit from it. But others soon repeated his method and published it.

climax.text: Phosphorus was the first element discovered by a known person. It opened the age of element hunting.

punchline.text: The first new element came from boiled urine. Science starts weird.

quiz.question: What was Hennig Brand originally trying to find when he discovered phosphorus?

details.summary: In 1669, Hamburg alchemist Hennig Brand became the first person to discover a chemical element through deliberate experiment when he isolated phosphorus from concentrated urine..
details.whyItMatters: Phosphorus was the first element discovered by a known individual, proving that undiscovered substances existed in common materials. This launched the systematic search for new elements that continues today.
takeaways: Brand processed over 5,500 liters of urine to isolate glowing phosphorus
Phosphorus was the first element whose discoverer and method are documented
The discovery proved that unknown elements could be isolated from everyday materials

faq.question: What made Brand decide to distill large quantities of urine?
faq.answer: As an alchemist seeking the philosopher's stone, Brand associated urine's golden color with gold. Alchemical theory suggested that organic fluids concentrated nature's vital essences..

faq.question: Why does phosphorus glow in the dark?
faq.answer: White phosphorus undergoes slow oxidation when exposed to air, reacting with oxygen at room temperature. This exothermic reaction excites the resulting phosphorus oxide molecules, which release energy as visible green-white light..
